$comment: Manual valve for the cross-provider availability heuristic in scripts/availability.ts.
Every deviation from the derivation lands here as a reviewable diff, because a wrong
merge is a runtime 404 rather than a validation error.
providers — the generation scope, listed explicitly rather than inferred from
src/providers/ (codegen must not depend on the filesystem layout). These are the 36
providers unmodel ships a chat validator for. cohere is absent on purpose: its chat
wire format is a fifth dialect with no translator in v1.
deny — edges the heuristic finds that must not ship. Each ref is "<provider>:<model-id>";
either half may use * as a wildcard. The edge is removed in both directions, and an
exact (glob-free) ref that matches nothing fails codegen so upstream renames surface.
force — equivalences the heuristic misses. Refs must be exact and must resolve to
in-scope chat rows; a force pair merges the two models' groups.
chatScopeExclude — rows removed from the three unmodel/chat ref tables because the
provider serves them on a different wire surface than its chat endpoint. models.dev
records modalities, not routes, so codegen cannot derive this. Same "<provider>:<id>"
spelling, and every entry must match at least one in-scope text model.
$targetOnlyNotes: Both are factory-configured (bedrock needs a region, azure a resource endpoint), so they are excluded from the one-argument .toApi union and their endpoint modules wire no api:. They stay in `providers` because other providers' rows legitimately target them — the data carries factory targets so the reserved two-argument overload needs no codegen change — but emitting a SOURCE table for them produced ~23 KB of generated code with no importer. Delete an entry here the day the matching endpoint module wires `api:`.

$denyNotes.azure:*claude*: azure lists 16 claude-* models but models.dev records api: null for azure and unmodel's azure module is OpenAI-compatible only. Nobody has verified which wire surface Azure exposes Claude on, so these rows ship no edges in either direction rather than a guessed dialect.
$denyNotes.google-vertex:*claude*: Vertex serves Claude through an Anthropic-shaped rawPredict surface that unmodel has no module for (models.dev also carries a separate google-vertex-anthropic provider unmodel does not implement). Deny until that endpoint exists; the google-vertex.chatRawPredict surface rule in scripts/availability.ts is already in place for when it does.
$denyNotes.google-vertex:mistral-*, google-vertex:c: Vertex serves Mistral's models (mistral-medium-3, mistral-small-2503, codestral-2 in the 2026-11-12 snapshot) on a publisher rawPredict route, not generateContent: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/mistral (checked 2026-11-12) documents "POST https:// LOCATION -aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/ PROJECT_ID /locations/ LOCATION /publishers/mistralai/models/ MODEL :rawPredict". unmodel has no module for that surface and these ids carry no -maas suffix, so without this pair the heuristic labels them google-vertex.chat (Gemini dialect, publishers/google URL). Deny until a mistralai rawPredict endpoint exists.

$chatScopeExcludeNotes.inception:mercury-edit-2: Served only on POST /v1/fim/completions and POST /v1/edit/completions — https://docs.inceptionlabs.ai/get-started/models lists "| **Mercury Edit 2** | … | `v1/fim/completions` `v1/edit/completions` |", and https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/edit/completions/models gives it "supported_endpoints":["edit.completions","fim.completions"], while https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/chat/completions/models omits it. POST /v1/chat/completions answers it 400 "Value error, Model must be one of the following: mercury, mercury-2, mercury-2.5, mercury-3, …" (checked 2026-11-13). models.dev files it as text-out, so without this entry the snapshot generates a chat ref that compiles to a 400. unmodel validates neither route; `checkChatRoute` in src/providers/inception/index.ts is the substrate twin. Substrate signpost warning, unified ref withdrawn.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:*-codex, openai:*-codex-*: gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5.3-codex-spark are served by POST /v1/responses only — developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.3-codex lists "Chat Completions | v1/chat/completions | Not supported" (checked 2026-08-26). unmodel/chat compiles Chat Completions and has no /v1/responses validator (docs/decisions.md #7), so a ref for these compiled a body the API refuses. The substrate keeps accepting them with a signpost warning naming the route; only the unified ref is withdrawn.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:gpt-daybreak-*: gpt-daybreak-blue-latest (alias of gpt-5.6-sol) and gpt-daybreak-red-latest (alias of gpt-5.6-cyber) are POST /v1/responses only — both model pages at developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-daybreak-{blue,red}-latest list "Chat Completions | v1/chat/completions | Not supported" and carry "Status: Deprecated" (checked 2026-11-12). models.dev files them as text-out with no status, so without this entry the 2026-11-12 snapshot generates a chat ref that compiles to a 400. Same treatment as codex: substrate signpost warning, unified ref withdrawn.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:*-pro: gpt-5-pro, gpt-5.2-pro, gpt-5.4-pro, gpt-5.5-pro, o1-pro and o3-pro are POST /v1/responses only — every model page at developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/{gpt-5-pro,gpt-5.2-pro,gpt-5.4-pro,gpt-5.5-pro,o1-pro,o3-pro} lists "| Chat Completions | `v1/chat/completions` | Not supported |" beside "| Responses | `v1/responses` | Supported |", and the prose agrees: "GPT-5.5 Pro is available for Responses API requests", "GPT-5.4 Pro is available in the Responses API only", "o3-pro is available in the Responses API only" (checked 2026-11-12). models.dev files them as text-out, so each shipped as a chat ref that compiles to a 400. Same treatment as codex: substrate signpost warning (`/-pro(?:$|-)/`), unified ref withdrawn. Only the bare-suffix glob is listed: no snapshot id carries `-pro-`, and an inert `*-pro-*` entry would fail codegen.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:text-embedding-*: Embeddings answer POST /v1/embeddings. models.dev files them as text-out, which is how they reached a chat ref table at all. Note the availability half already drops them on the billing signal in scripts/availability.ts (`isChatRow`) — this list is what the weaker `isTextModel` in chatScope needs.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:gpt-image-*, openai:chatgpt-image: Image generation answers POST /v1/images/generations, which is `image` from unmodel/openai. They are text-out in models.dev because they accept and echo text.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.openai:gpt-realtime-*: The realtime family answers the WebRTC/WebSocket realtime API, not chat/completions.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.mistral:mistral-embed: An embeddings model: it answers POST /v1/embeddings — https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-embed-23-12 lists "Features Embeddings /v1/embeddings" (checked 2026-11-12). models.dev files it as text-out (type "embedding"), which is how it reached a chat ref table at all.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.mistral:voxtral-mini-latest: Transcription only: the card lists `"names":["voxtral-mini-2602","voxtral-mini-latest"]` and features only "Timestamps /v1/audio/transcriptions Transcriptions /v1/audio/transcriptions" (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/voxtral-mini-transcribe-26-02, checked 2026-11-12) — that is `stt` from unmodel/mistral. The chat-capable Voxtral Mini 25.07 retired 5/31/2026 (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models); models.dev types the alias "transcription" and still files it as text-out.
$chatScopeExcludeNotes.$scope: The openai entries mirror `NonChatModelId` in src/providers/openai/chat.ts, which states the same eight families as a TYPE (so it can shape `OpenaiChatModelId`) and therefore cannot be read by codegen. `test/chat/refs.test.ts` asserts the two agree. `dall-e-*` is in the type and deliberately absent here: models.dev files DALL·E as image-out only, so `isTextModel` already excludes it and an entry would be inert — and inert entries fail codegen. The mistral entries are mistral's own: the two text-out rows models.dev types "embedding" and "transcription".
